validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: both endpoints are independently real. Gazli (Bukhara Region) is the well-documented Soviet-era gas hub/field (ru.wikipedia Uztransgaz article, gsg.spb.ru Bukhara-Ural history, gazligs.com Gazli UGS partner pages). Sarymay is a genuine populated place in Xorazm (Khorezm) Region, confirmed by TWO sources with zero connection to GEM: (1) a Uzbek presidential decree text hosted by FAO's legal database (faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/uzb197238.pdf) which lists 'Сарымай' among Khorezm-region settlements and separately itemizes a 2016-2019, $274.2m, 220kV power line project 'Tahiatash TES - PS Khorezm - settlement Sarymay (Khorezm region)'; (2) an EBRD-financed 'Sarimay-Djankeldy Transmission' project (ebrd.com/home/work-with-us/projects/psd/52874.html, board-approved 2022-09-21, disbursing as of 2025-07-10) building a 128 km 500kV line between Sarimay (Khorezm) and Djankeldy (Bukhara Region) plus expanding the Sarimay substation -- i.e. an internationally financed, currently-active infrastructure corridor running the SAME Bukhara-to-Khorezm direction GEM records for this gas line. This is strong corroboration the corridor and endpoint are real, even though that specific EBRD/decree evidence is about POWER transmission, not gas -- flagged so it is never mistaken for gas-pipeline sourcing. Uztransgaz's own corporate-structure filing (utg.uz/upload/medialibrary/378/3782e1330a84effbfd65bf5ba92cb363.pdf, HTTP 200, table of 'structural subdivisions' listing UP "Urgenchtransgaz" in Khorezm region/Urgench alongside "Gazliyskoe UMG" in Bukhara region/Gazli) independently confirms Uztransgaz maintains separate trunk-pipeline directorates in exactly these two regions -- consistent with a Gazli-origin trunk line reaching into Khorezm, though the filing does not name this pipeline by segment. NOTE: the PDF's Cyrillic text failed url_verifier's substring screen (a known false-negative class per the verifier's own docs for PDFs) -- confirmed manually with `pdftotext` (text 'Ургенчтрансгаз' / 'Газлийское УМГ' both present, page fetches HTTP 200) before relying on it; not cited as a fills ref because it does not name the pipeline itself, only the regional org structure. SPEC (Length 103 km, Diameter 1220 mm, sections 0-56 km / 56-103 km, shareholders Uzbekneftegaz/Tashneftegazstroy/Bukharagneftegazstroy/Yuggazstroy/Mubareknefte gazmontazh/Uztransgaz): this exact figure set, matching GEM's own Length=103.00 km and Diameter=1220 mm precisely, surfaced consistently across MULTIPLE independent search passes, all tracing to gem.wiki's own cited source ngm.uz/ru/page/view/22 (Neftegazmontazh, a construction contractor site independent of GEM). I could NOT independently verify this live: the whole ngm.uz domain (root, /ru, /en paths all tested) returned a genuine HTTP 503 'the server is temporarily unable to service your request due to maintenance downtime or capacity problems' -- confirmed identically via direct curl AND via an independent r.jina.ai proxy fetch (different network path, same 503+message), which rules out a block aimed at us specifically. Its Wayback capture (20250905224526) exists per the availability API but web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this environment throughout this session (repeated timeouts, one bare 200 with no body retrievable) -- the same documented network condition already on file for this batch (utg.uz/ru/about/history/ case), not evidence about the source. So: strong circumstantial + repeated-snippet corroboration for the spec values, zero contradiction from any source, but NO url_verifier-passing citation obtainable today for Length/Diameter/Construction/Start -- left UNRESOLVED rather than cited, per standing rule 2. CLASSIFICATION: 1220mm trunk from a major gas hub to a regional terminus is a normal transmission-class line; PipelineType=transmission is correct, no basis to flag. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 18-row roster -- no other row's endpoints touch Sarymay or Xorazm Region; the other Gazli-origin siblings (P2290/P3983/P3984 Gazli-Kagan, P4073 Gazli-Nukus) are named, differently-terminated pipes with no source describing any of them as identical to this one. Not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Uztransgaz 100% is consistent with Uztransgaz's role, independently confirmed via its own current site (utg.uz/en/, verified OK), as Uzbekistan's sole state gas-transport/transit/export company -- generic (not segment-specific) but directly on-point; staged as a low-tier fill below. FuelSource=Gazli is internally consistent with every other Gazli-* pipeline in the roster (P2290/P3983/P3984/P4073) and is not contradicted by anything found.

Circumstantial evidence of continued regional activity in the same Bukhara-Khorezm corridor: the EBRD-financed Sarimay-Djankeldy 500kV power project (board-approved 2022-09-21) is listed as 'Disbursing' as of its most recent update, 2025-07-10 -- confirming ongoing infrastructure investment through Sarimay as recently as mid-2025, though that is an electricity project, not this gas line, so it is corroborating context only, not a status-change source. Uztransgaz (utg.uz, live site, 2026) continues to operate as Uzbekistan's sole gas-transport company with no indication of asset retirements in this corridor. A December 2023 EADaily report on winter pipeline failures in Uzbekistan mentions repair work near Gazli (Bukhara Region) and in Urgench District (Khorezm Region) but does not name this specific trunk line. Given a domestic transmission trunk under a state monopoly with no negative signal anywhere, and the absence of any evidence of change, 'confirm' with a general-context evidence date of 2025-07 rather than a segment-specific one. Under the sweep's threshold, this is not stale enough to trigger dormancy rules (line reads as an actively-maintained operating asset, not a proposed/shelved one).
